newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain overshot social security deficit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Spain overshot social security deficit in 1996.

text.p: Spain overshot its social security deficit target in 1996, with the deficit coming in at around 0.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Social Security Secretary Juan Carlos Aparicio said on Friday.
He said the 1996 deficit was lower than in 1995, when it was 0.73 percent of GDP, but still higher than the 0.3 percent target.

"We'll achieve an intermediate position (between the two figures), or little lower, with an substantial fall in comparison with the previous year, and what is important is that we met the overall (public deficit) target of 4.4 percent," he told Reuters in a interview.
Spain's central government deficit was 3.3 percent of GDP in 1996, undershooting the initial target of 3.5 percent. 1996 GDP equals 74.4 trillion pesetas.
The 1996 social security deficit could be "around 0.5 percent," Aparicio said.

Press reports have said the 1996 social security deficit was 372.6 billion pesetas, but Aparecio declined to comment on this, except to say that this year the social security deficit will be lower than that.
"There is a new framework, which would explain the target for further reductions (in 1997) than in 1996," he said.
Spain forecast in its 1997 budget that it would squeeze the number to 0.2 percent of GDP this year.
He added Spain is introducing measures, among others, against social security fraud and default in payments vis a vis collecting old debts from both private and public firms.
